overall: Atlanta hit a running maximum of 87.8°F today, surpassing all NWP model forecasts (ECMWF=85.1, HRRR=86.0, NBM=86.0) and even the intraday model's central expectation. Temperatures peaked around 17:04 ET and have since declined to 84.2°F by 18:52 ET, with velocity flat to negative and the trajectory clearly past the daily apex. No active alerts or severe weather complicated the picture today — conditions were typical late-spring convective, with afternoon scattered clouds (SCT, ~62% cloud fraction) doing little to suppress peak heating.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models (85.1–86.0°F) meaningfully underforecast today's high; the observed running max of 87.8°F runs roughly 1.8–2.7°F above model consensus. The META bucket distribution had its mass split across 86–87F, 88–89F, and 90–91F, and the intraday model was anchored around 86–87F — both somewhat consistent with the actual outcome landing in the upper half of the 86–88°F range, but no single model nailed the overshoot.
max_temp_prediction: With the daily peak recorded at approximately 17:04 ET and current temperature declining to 84.2°F at 18:52 ET, the daily high is effectively locked in. The running max of 87.8°F is the best available estimate of TMAX, and there is near-zero probability of further warming this late in the evening given the downward velocity trend and approaching sunset. The give-up classifier fired at hour 15.92 when running max was 86.0°F, yet temperatures continued to push higher — reinforcing that 87.8°F is the true day's peak. Confidence is very high (>95%) that today's TMAX lands at or within 0.2°F of 87.8°F.
